For inference efficiency, we provide here a theoretical derivation for the compression ratio of our
method. Since we only add an extra visual decoder after the modality connector compared to the
original model, we ignore the computational cost of the ViT and the modality connector, and only
consider the LLM. Furthermore, we focus only on the main overhead—the matrix multiplications
within the Attention and MLP modules—while ignoring the text embedding, Softmax, activation
functions, and the final language head.
Assume the LLM has L layers, the model dimension is d, and the intermediate dimension of the
MLP is d′. The visual decoder φ has a size of Rd×|V|, where V is the vocabulary. We consider
the input of a single image, where the visual sequence length is n, and we ignore the length of the
instruction. The computational cost of the original model is:
C = (8nd2 + 4n2d + 4ndd′)L
(FLOPs)
When the compression ratio is r, the computational cost of our method is:
C′ = [8n(1 −r)d2 + 4n2(1 −r)2d + 4n(1 −r)dd′]L + 2nd|V|
(FLOPs)
Therefore, we can measure inference efficiency by C′
C . For LLaVA-1.5-7B, the compression ratio r
of our method can reach 0.58, corresponding to C′
C = 43.82%, which is highly efficient.
